extracted.intended_audience: absolute beginners learning French (A1), self-study learners and travelers
extracted.subtask_description: A step-by-step guide for absolute-beginner learners to reach A1 proficiency or survive a trip to France, covering pronunciation, core verbs, basic grammar, essential vocabulary, audio practice, and a 14-day study plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Begin with pronunciation / Master pronunciation
rubrics_metrics.description: Start with pronunciation so every word sticks; learn the French alphabet with audio and the 30 Reading Rules so spelling maps to sound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand accents (acute é and grave è) (see accents overview). Practice ENT endings, the EU in 'heure', and liaison rules. Every lesson features authentic audio recorded by a professional native French voice artist so you learn the right way to speak from day one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build your first sentences
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn the minimal grammar and phrases needed to create short, correct sentences and simple interactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover greetings (Bonjour, Salut, Ça va), subject pronouns (je, tu, il/elle, nous, vous, ils/elles), articles (un, une, le, la, les, des), question forms (est-ce que, inversion, question words), negation (ne… pas and other common forms), and when to use tu vs vous. See linked lessons (greetings overview, est-ce que lesson) for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learn the four essential verbs
rubrics_metrics.description: Master four high-utility verbs in present tense that underpin much beginner communication: être, avoir, aller, faire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Être — to be (present tense, describe people and things). Avoir — to have (and phrases like avoir peur or avoir faim). Aller — to go (talk about plans or movement). Faire — to do or make (daily life, hobbies, weather). After these, progress to parler, prendre, mettre, venir, pouvoir, vouloir, savoir, connaître, devoir. Explore the Top 100 French Verbs and their full conjugation tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present tense practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Practice core verbs in the present tense to build fluency in everyday speech.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work with 25 verbs in the present tense. Start with regular -er, -ir, and -re verbs (see regular verbs guide). Speak each one aloud until it feels natural.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build everyday vocabulary / Core beginner topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Acquire practical vocabulary sets that support daily interactions and basic descriptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study numbers 1–100, days of the week, months, how to say the year, telling time, weather expressions (il fait beau, il pleut), ordering food & restaurant phrases, how to ask directions, distinctions like C’est vs il est, family, clothing, colors, feelings, sports, hobbies, travel words, and adjectives (how they work). Use the complete vocabulary hub for organized lists and drills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use authentic audio and music
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage audio materials and songs to internalize pronunciation, rhythm, and common phrases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Word of the Day for daily audio and examples. Explore beginner-friendly songs (Alouette, Frère Jacques, La Vie en rose) via the Top 20 French Songs guide and use the Song Lyrics Hub to study lyrics and listen repeatedly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow a simple 14-day roadmap
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a compact, time-boxed plan to structure initial learning and cover essential beginner topics in two weeks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Days 1–2: Alphabet, accents, reading rules, liaison. Day 3: Greetings, pronouns, articles. Day 4: Être + short descriptions. Day 5: Avoir + phrases (avoir faim, soif, peur). Day 6: Aller + plans and places. Day 7: Faire + routines and weather. Day 8: Questions (est-ce que / inversion) + negation. Day 9: Numbers, days, months, time. Day 10: Family words + adjectives. Day 11: Ordering meals in restaurants. Day 12: Clothing, colors, shopping basics. Day 13: Directions and transport. Day 14: Review with three quizzes + seven recent Words of the Day lessons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice habits: short daily study and scheduled practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt compact, consistent study sessions to build momentum and retention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study 15 minutes at a scheduled time. Practice daily with the Word of the Day and short quizzes. Keep a streak and make study habitual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active production: speak and repeat aloud
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize speaking and active repetition over passive review to make language 'stick'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read every example out loud. Speak each verb and phrase aloud until natural. Play the audio over and over again. Don't worry about perfection—focus on producing speech.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set small goals and retention targets
rubrics_metrics.description: Use achievable short-term goals and measurable word targets to sustain progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set small short-term goals and stick to them. Keep a streak: one Word of the Day + five new words daily. Make sure you really master the core verbs before moving on.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use bundled resources and corrective materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplement lessons with targeted resources that address common errors and provide structured practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Download the free Beginner PDF '20 Common French Mistakes (and How to Fix Them)'. Explore the Top 100 French Verbs and full conjugation tables, regular verbs guide, vocabulary hub, and suggested paid course (À Moi Paris) if you want guided lessons starting at A1.
